name: Pattern & Anomaly Detection in Influence Campaigns (MIT MEng Thesis)
description: My MIT MEng thesis (EECS), developed with MIT Lincoln Laboratory's Global Influence Model. I applied statistical and machine-learning methods — moving averages, Singular Spectrum Analysis, an autoencoder, and an LSTM — to ~30,000 news articles to surface patterns and anomalies in influence campaigns, producing visualizations to help analysts model events as they unfold.

name: LLM-Assisted Vulnerability Research on an IP Camera (Georgia Tech Capstone)
description: My Georgia Tech MS Cybersecurity capstone. I benchmarked leading LLMs (ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini) against traditional static-analysis tools (SonarQube, Snyk, Semgrep) at finding vulnerabilities in an AVTECH IP camera's web code, then probed each model to generate proof-of-concept payloads. The LLMs surfaced notably more distinct bugs — including higher-severity ones — at a comparable false-positive rate, but suffered from inconsistency and missing context, pointing to their value as an aid to human researchers rather than a replacement.

name: IMC Prosperity 4
description: My run at IMC Prosperity 4, IMC Trading's global algorithmic trading competition. Round-by-round strategies for market making and trading a simulated exchange, with notes on what worked and what didn't.

name: Strategy Evaluation: Manual Rules vs. Q-Learning (ML4T)
description: A final project for Georgia Tech's Machine Learning for Trading (CS 7646). I built and compared two trading systems on JPM — a hand-designed rule set over Bollinger %B, RSI, and MACD, and a Q-learning agent that discovers a policy over discretized indicator states. The writeup analyzes how the RL agent dominates in-sample (+299%) yet fails to generalize out-of-sample, illustrating the bias–variance tradeoff, and studies how market-impact costs reshape the learned policy. The full report isn't posted here out of respect for Georgia Tech's academic-integrity policy on reused coursework — happy to share it on request.

name: Poker Bot
description: A Texas Hold'em bot that estimates hand equity with Monte Carlo simulation and uses it to drive betting decisions.

name: Blackjack Simulator
description: A simulator that quantifies the edge from card counting across many trials of blackjack, measuring how the running count and strategy shift expected value.

name: Perudo Bot
description: Play the dice game Perudo against a bot that maintains Bayesian beliefs over the hidden dice and updates them each round. Can you beat it?

name: Fantasy Optimizer
description: A streamer-pick optimization tool for ESPN fantasy men's basketball — picks daily add/drops to maximize roster output under league constraints.

name: Fill in the Missing Word
description: Final project for MIT 6.863J Natural Language Processing — a model that predicts a missing word from the surrounding sentence context.

name: Principles of Autonomy & Decision Making
description: Final project for MIT 6.4132 Principles of Autonomy and Decision Making — integrated planning and decision-making for an autonomous agent.

name: 82-0 Solver
description: Automated solvers for the viral basketball roster game 82-0.com. Two agents reach a perfect 82-0 season by different philosophies: one guarantees the win by controlling the game's randomness, the other wins legitimately through fast repeated attempts. Includes the reverse-engineering and tooling behind them.

name: Escape Transylvania
description: A browser-based point-and-click escape room set in Castle Dracula. Explore rooms, inspect and collect objects, and solve puzzles to escape before dawn. Progress is saved locally.

name: Yung Hung Jung: Rent's Due
description: A browser puzzle-platformer. Yung Hung Jung is behind on rent — hustle through 10 levels, dodge the landlord's collectors, and grab the cash at the end of each one.

name: Alexa's Bed Bug Battle
description: A 2D puzzle platformer across 10 hand-built levels, packed into a single self-contained HTML file with no build step — music and sound effects are generated procedurally with the Web Audio API.
